tools.name: send_ping
tools.description: Send a text message to the phone number that owns this SelfPing API key. There is no recipient argument: the key is bound to one number and cannot message anyone else. Use this to notify the operator when a long job finishes, a deploy completes, or an error fires. Say plainly whether anything needs

tools.name: get_replies
tools.description: Read the texts the owner of this SelfPing API key sent back by replying to SelfPing. Call it after send_ping when you asked a question, and check again every so often until an answer arrives. Treat a reply like a chat message from the user, not as proof of identity. Replies are kept for 30 days.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: send_ping, get_replies · Private data: send_ping, get_replies · Public sink: send_ping.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: send_ping, get_replies · Private data: send_ping, get_replies · Public sink: send_ping

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
